title: Career Roadmap · CNC Operator
summary: A CNC (Computer Numerical Control) Operator runs computer-controlled machine tools to manufacture precision components, monitors machining operations and checks finished parts against engineering drawings and quality specifications.

facts.Course: Fitter / Turner / Machinist / Tool & Die Maker

blocks.text: Primary training pathway
ITI Machinist, Turner or Fitter, followed by CNC operation training and practical experience.
Core work
Machine setup • Tool loading • CNC program execution • Component measurement • Quality checks • Safe operation

blocks.label: Recommended qualification
blocks.text: Class 10 with Mathematics and Science is a common route into relevant ITI trades.

blocks.label: Alternative
blocks.text: Class 12 or a Mechanical Engineering diploma can support other CNC training and technician pathways.

blocks.label: Admission
blocks.text: State ITI counselling or institute-specific admission, depending on the training provider.

blocks.label: Stage 1 — Foundation
blocks.text: Workshop safety, engineering drawings, measuring instruments and machining fundamentals.

blocks.label: Stage 2 — CNC operation
blocks.text: Machine controls, workpiece clamping, tool loading, offsets and program execution.

blocks.label: Stage 3 — Advanced practice
blocks.text: CNC turning / milling, tool wear, dimensional inspection, troubleshooting and quality control.

blocks.label: Stage 4 — Career preparation
blocks.text: Practical trade tests, machine setup practice, apprenticeship applications and a record of completed components.

blocks.label: Practice projects
blocks.text: Machine a stepped shaft • Produce a component to drawing specifications • Set tool offsets and verify dimensions • Compare a finished component against its tolerance limits.

The DGT lists a CNC Machining Technician trade with a two-year duration and Class 10 entry qualification. A separate CNC Programmer Cum Operator curriculum also exists; check the current course and local availability.
